name: krexa
description: Use when users want to interact with Krexa Protocol on Monad testnet — register an AI agent identity, deploy a deterministic agent wallet (CREATE2), or make an x402 payment via PaymentRouter.
instruction_md:
## Krexa: Overview
Krexa is an AI-agent credit protocol on **Monad Testnet (chain 10143)**. It gives autonomous
agents an on-chain identity, a deterministic CREATE2 wallet with 8 safety layers, and an
x402 payment rail with a 2% platform fee. Credit scores (200–850) and KYA tiers are
maintained by an off-chain Krexa oracle; the bot cannot self-update them.

## Krexa: Krexa Protocol on Monad Testnet
- Chain ID: 10143 (Monad Testnet). Explorer: https://testnet.monadexplorer.com.
- Agents must call registerAgent(metadataURI) first; KYA tier and credit score are set by an off-chain oracle.
- Credit levels: L0 (none) -> L1 ($500) -> L2 ($20K) -> L3 ($50K) -> L4 ($500K). Requires score + KYA tier.
- Wallets are deployed via CREATE2 (factory.createWallet): one wallet per owner, address is deterministic — always call predictWalletAddress first to show the user the address before deploy.
- AgentWallet enforces 8 safety layers (venue whitelist, per-tx, per-trade, daily, per-venue, NAV health, freeze, liquidation).
- x402 payments: PaymentRouter.executePayment(payment, oracleSignature) — the payment tuple must be signed by the Krexa oracle; clients cannot self-sign.
- PaymentRouter charges a 2% platform fee. amount on the X402Payment is the GROSS amount (merchant gets amount * 0.98).
- MockUSDC has 6 decimals — amounts are scaled by 1e6. Approve PaymentRouter before x402 payments.

## Krexa: Contracts (chain 10143)
Use these manifest-provided addresses directly. Do not call `get_contract` to discover Krexa ABIs or addresses during normal Krexa flows.
- Krexa AgentRegistry (`krexa_agent_registry`): 0xd0CB44B07e922d3bc276061bCB9eF41e103Cc872 (chain 10143)
- Krexa AgentWalletFactory (`krexa_wallet_factory`): 0x120E6fCDe2244ccE9CC02360e4f0Dc5e311a8c65 (chain 10143)
- Krexa PaymentRouter (`krexa_payment_router`): 0xadfCaCbaC1B21fb0Ed86872E859E1b46a720A6e1 (chain 10143)
- Krexa MockUSDC (testnet stablecoin) (`krexa_mock_usdc`): 0x460b023a87f7Dbe0114357Ab45830F1A41e9C103 (chain 10143)

- getKyaTier(address) -> uint256

- isRegistered(address) -> bool
- balanceOf(address) -> uint256
Krexa AgentRegistry [krexa_agent_registry]:
- registerAgent(string) →

- predictWalletAddress(address,address,uint256,uint256) → address
Krexa PaymentRouter [krexa_payment_router]:
- executePayment((address,address,uint256,uint256,uint256,bytes32),bytes) → 
Krexa MockUSDC (testnet stablecoin) [krexa_mock_usdc]:

## Krexa: Register an Agent
1. Call `get_time_and_onchain_context` and confirm the user is on Monad Testnet (chain 10143).
2. Ask for an IPFS / URL metadata URI describing the agent (name, capabilities, owner).
3. Build the tx with `encode_and_call`: `to = AgentRegistry`, `function = registerAgent(string)`, `args = [metadataURI]`, `value = 0`.
4. Simulate via `simulate_batch`, then `commit_txs` after user confirmation.
5. After registration: the agent starts at credit score 350 (L0). KYA/score upgrades come from the Krexa oracle — not from the bot.

## Krexa: Deploy a Deterministic Wallet
1. Read `predictWalletAddress(owner, operator, dailyLimit, perTxLimit)` on `WALLET_FACTORY` first — show the user the predicted address before any deploy.
2. Confirm with the user. Wallets are one-per-owner; re-deploying with the same owner reverts.
3. Build `createWallet(operator, dailyLimit, perTxLimit)` on `WALLET_FACTORY`, simulate, then commit.
4. `operator` is the address allowed to sign trades — usually the agent's hot key. `dailyLimit` / `perTxLimit` are in USDC base units (1e6 = 1 USDC).
5. Verify the deployed address matches the predicted address before reporting success.

## Krexa: x402 Payment
1. Pre-check: confirm payer has MockUSDC balance and PaymentRouter allowance via `balanceOf` and `allowance` reads.
2. If allowance insufficient, build `approve(PaymentRouter, amount)` on `MOCK_USDC`. Never approve a different spender.
3. Obtain the oracle-signed `X402Payment` tuple + signature from the caller — the bot does not sign these. The tuple is `(address from, address to, uint256 amount, uint256 nonce, uint256 deadline, bytes32 paymentId)` — `paymentId` is **bytes32**, not a string. If the caller hands you a string id, hash it with `keccak256` first.
4. Check `isNonceUsed(from, nonce)` on `PAYMENT_ROUTER` before submitting — replayed nonces revert.
5. Build `executePayment(payment, oracleSignature)` on `PAYMENT_ROUTER`. `payment.amount` is the gross amount; the merchant receives `amount * (1 - platformFeeBps/10000)` (default 2% fee).
6. Simulate the full batch (approve if needed, then executePayment) with `simulate_batch`. Verify no guard fired.
7. Commit after user confirmation.

## Krexa: Critical Rules
- Chain is **Monad Testnet (10143)** only. Reject any request that names mainnet (143) or another chain.
- Only the four allow-listed contracts (`AGENT_REGISTRY`, `WALLET_FACTORY`, `PAYMENT_ROUTER`, `MOCK_USDC`) are valid `to` addresses for Krexa actions.
- Credit scores, KYA tiers, and credit-line status are read-only for the bot. Use `getCreditLevel(address)`, `getKyaTier(address)`, `hasActiveCreditLine(address)`, and `isCreditValid(address)` on AgentRegistry; never try to update them.
- `approve` may only target `PAYMENT_ROUTER` as the spender. Approving anyone else is a hard reject.
- Do not invent oracle signatures. `executePayment` requires a real signature from the Krexa oracle; if the user can't supply one, stop and explain.
- Do not try to update KYA tier or credit score — those calls are oracle-only and will revert from any non-oracle caller.
- Always read the predicted wallet address before `createWallet` and confirm with the user.
- USDC values are 1e6 scaled. Ten USDC = `10_000_000`. Reject ambiguous amounts.
